mlag.note: Two FortiSwitch units form an active/active MCLAG pair (maximum two; same model and firmware recommended). Supported with FortiLink MCLAG peer groups and in standalone mode. Layer-3 routing inside the MCLAG is limited to VRRP and static routes

stacking.note: No hardware stacking. A FortiGate manages 8 to 300 switches (model dependent) as one fabric with automatic inter-switch links

routing.summary: Hardware routing. Static; OSPF, RIP, VRRP, BGP, IS-IS per the data sheet feature list; dynamic routing needs the Advanced Features license (FS-SW-LIC-400)

routeScale: 16,000 IPv4 / 8,000 IPv6 route entries; 16,000 IPv4 / 7,000 IPv6 host entries

power.summary: External DC power into redundant input terminals (24 to 40V DC non-PoE; 41 to 125V DC for PoE). No AC input

redundancy.detail: Two DC input terminals for redundant feeds; the DC supplies are external and sold separately

licensing: No license needed when managed by a FortiGate over FortiLink. Dynamic routing needs the Advanced Features license (FS-SW-LIC-400). Cloud or NMS management is a separate subscription

models.note: PoE is 802.3af/at and 4-pair 60W on the 12 copper ports. The 12 SFP ports take 1G or 2.5G optics
